findings.title: attributed failed equivalence
findings.claim: The counted coins can stage a failed equation: the verse displays a monetary counterpart and simultaneously marks that counterpart as deficient.
findings.mechanism: The supplied HFT trace carries counterpart imagery at the exchange surface and is independently triggered by the price, deficiency, and counted amount; their contact makes the proposed equivalence visible and then breaks it inside the pricing phrase.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the coins as an attempted measure of a person and the deficient adjective as the word that invalidates the equation.
findings.containment: The ordinary few-coin sale remains recoverable; this attributed equivalence reading is local pressure, not a replacement or rank.

findings.title: attributed withdrawn stewardship
findings.claim: The sellers' lack of desire can be heard as withdrawal from stewardship, with the cheap exchange transferring both custody and concern away.
findings.mechanism: The supplied HFT trace carries the stewardship relation through the copular surface and is independently triggered by the exchange and diminished amount; their contact changes detached valuation into a local image of relinquished responsibility.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the low-price transfer as withdrawal from keeping or standing for the person, alongside its ordinary commercial sense.
findings.containment: The ordinary copular class verdict and cheap sale remain primary; this attributed reading does not invent a lexical gloss for كَانُوا or claim stewardship is the only sense.
